Subject: HelixAI: capacity runway & switchover timing

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're preparing our commit to Reserved capacity and need Redwood's sizing validation and a practical switchover timeline aligned to our deal cadence. High-level asks: 
- Confirm GPU-type and shard counts for a baseline commit (we expect sustained 3.2k QPS at 1.2k token avg across peak windows)
- Outline a staged switchover (canary + ramp) with rollback gates and expected latency impact
- Confirm blackout windows and required runbook owners for the cutover

I've attached a sample traffic model (peak/90th/avg by hour) and a spreadsheet with proposed commit amounts. Can you respond with a recommended runway and target dates? We aim to be on Dedicated in late Sept if feasible.

Thanks,
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Platform Engineering
HelixAI

Attachment: helix_traffic_model.json (traffic sample, anonymized)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Cc: ops@helixai.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixAI: capacity runway & switchover timing

Hi Maria —

Appreciate the data. Quick answers up front: based on the traffic snapshot, the baseline we recommend is a 3-shard design on A100s (8-way concurrency estimate) with an initial buffer of ~15% headroom for burst protection. That maps to the attached commit matrix (helix_commit_matrix_v3.xlsx) with suggested reserved GPU counts and a staged activation plan.

Key assumptions we used (please confirm):
- Sustained peak QPS: 3.2k
- Avg tokens per request: 1.2k
- Cache/prefix hit rate: 28% (we can tune aggressively in staging)
- Expected 95th latency target: <200ms token tail on A100 config

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- Sept 20: Dedicated pool commissioned in staging (no customer traffic)
- Sept 22: Internal canary (10% synthetic + traffic replay for 4 hours)
- Sept 24: Customer canary (10% real traffic for 2 hours) -> ramp to 50% after 6 hours if metrics stable -> 100% after 24 hours

Blackout / rollback: we recommend a 4-hour rollback window after each ramp step with automatic fallback to hosted if error rates exceed +2% absolute or latency regression >30% relative.

Can you confirm the cache assumptions and whether Helix can accept the Sept 20 staging date? I'll loop in our capacity/ops leads to validate the commit matrix.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Attachment: helix_commit_matrix_v3.xlsx

Forwarding Helix's ask — Monica / Jordan, can you validate the baseline A100 x3-shard recommendation and run a quick throughput sim against the attached traffic model? Specific asks: 
- Run 95th/99th latency sims and 30-min burst scenarios (x2 baseline QPS)
- Monte Carlo over cache-hit variance +/-10% and token length +/-20%
- Confirm fallback behavior & estimate cost delta if we add an additional shard for safety

Also paste any operational runbook steps we should include in the customer-facing switchover doc (who owns killswitch, how we rotate keys, how we confirm cache priming).

Thanks,
Olga

Subject: Re: Fwd: HelixAI: capacity runway & switchover timing (internal validation)

Quick validation notes from infra sims: 
- With the provided traffic profile, 3 A100 shards meet baseline throughput but the 95th token latency approaches target under sustained bursts. We recommend either +15% capacity (add one A100) or convert to a 2x A10 cluster with more shards if Helix prefers lower-cost hardware (tradeoff: slightly higher latency tail).
- Monte Carlo with cache-hit +/-10% shows tail sensitivity; adding the extra shard reduces 99th latency by ~18%.
- For canary cadence, propose: synthetic replay (10%) -> customer canary (10%) -> 50% ramp -> 100% over 24 hrs. Each ramp step with a 4-hr auto rollback gate.

Operational runbook bullets to include in the customer doc: 
- Pre-cutover: KMS key check, model artifact checksum, KV cache priming (replay warmers)
- Canary: Enable traffic mirror & tracing, monitor 95/99 latencies and error-rate, validate model outputs on sample prompts
- Rollback: Toggle routing to hosted endpoint (infra playbook), drain KV caches, revert autoscaler to hosted thresholds
- Owners: Jordan (infra killswitch + routing), Monica (load validation + metrics), Olga (customer comms)

Attachment: helix_traffic_model.json (annotated with sim results)

Monica Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Final: HelixAI dedicated runway, staging velocity and switchover schedule

Maria / Helix ops —

Thanks for the patience. Based on our validation runs the team and Helix agree to the following plan:

Agreed commit (baseline): 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (3 baseline + 1 buffer) in a dedicated pool. See commit matrix attached.

Switchover schedule (final):
- Sept 20 (08:00 PT): Dedicated pool commissioned and smoke tests (no customer traffic)
- Sept 22 (09:00 PT): Synthetic canary & traffic replay (10% equivalent for 4 hours)
- Sept 24 (10:00 PT): Customer canary 10% real traffic for 2 hours -> if stable, ramp to 50% after 6 hours -> 100% after 24 hours

Rollback gates: Automatic fallback to hosted if error-rate increase >2% absolute or 95th-latency regressions >30% relative. Each ramp step has a 4-hour rollback window. Jordan will own killswitch actions; Monica will own validation metrics; Olga will coordinate customer comms and escalation.

Pre-cutover checklist (high level):
- Confirm DocuSign executed for Reserved commit (Ops/Legal)
- KMS access validated and key rotation window confirmed
- Replay warmers primed 24h before customer canary
- Pager routing and on-call readout distributed to Helix and Redwood SREs

Next steps: 
1) Maria — confirm DocuSign status and confirm you accept the Sept 20 staging date.
2) Ops@helixai — provide final KMS contact and preferred on-call pager for Sept 20–25.
3) Redwood: we'll upload the customer-facing runbook to the shared drive and send the DocuSign link.
